title: Jaguar makes epic 2100-kilometre journey across the Amazon | New Scientist
description: A jaguar that has been dubbed Gaspar traversed 2100 kilometres of the Amazon, crossing farms and roads. But why he set off on this mission is unclear
author: Joshua Rapp Learn

title: Matcha is under threat from climate change – can genomics save it? | New Scientist
description: Climate change is affecting the yields and flavour of the traditional Japanese tea matcha, but studying its seedlings' genetic tolerance for heat could future-proof the crop
author: Michael Fitzpatrick

title: Asteroid strike caused global firestorm that incinerated the dinosaurs | New Scientist
description: After the Chicxulub impact 66 million years ago, trillions of tonnes of rock vapour was launched into space before falling back to Earth at ballistic speeds, creating a global blast of heat strong enough to broil life on land
author: James Woodford

title: Unprecedented 'fire clouds' are fanning the flames in France | New Scientist
description: Flame-generated thunderstorms known as pyrocumulonimbus clouds can make wildfires even more intense, and they are expected to become more common in Europe
author: Alec Luhn

title: Mystery hominin left big footprints at ancient lake in Africa | New Scientist
description: Over 1.4 million years ago, a group of eight ancient hominins walked across a shallow mudflat, but their footprints don’t match those of Paranthropus boisei or Homo erectus
author: James Woodford

title: We’ve found the best example yet of an enormous wandering black hole | New Scientist
description: Astronomers have caught a supermassive black hole straying far from the centre of its galaxy using light from a star being ripped apart
author: Leah Crane
